title: Faction fight: How Europeans can better influence American foreign policy battles – European Council on Foreign Relations
gist: Majda Ruge argues US foreign policy under Trump is a hybrid of restrainer, prioritiser and primacist agendas that hurts Europe most — cutting Ukraine support while a primacist-driven Iran war spikes European energy prices. A summer 2026 Pentagon questionnaire to NATO allies mixed burden-shifting with demands to buy American and back the Iran war, but the Iran war has also raised Europe's leverage over the 2026 US force-posture review, which Europeans squandered by sending 27 separate responses.

themes.theme: Three tribes and Trump's hybrid foreign policy

insights.claim: Three foreign policy 'tribes' compete for Trump's ear — restrainers (full US retrenchment), prioritisers (focus on Asia) and primacists (continued global primacy) — and none has fully implemented its vision, producing policy through presidential improvisation and semi-autonomous bureaucratic agendas.
insights.speaker: Majda Ruge
insights.so_what: US policy toward Europe is volatile and faction-dependent, making transatlantic security commitments hard to forecast.
insights.quote: Three foreign policy “tribes” compete for President Donald Trump’s ear: restrainers, prioritisers and primacists.

insights.claim: On Ukraine and European security Trump leans toward restrainers and prioritisers by cutting Ukraine support and doing business with Russia, while primacists prevailed on Iran — leaving Europe with skyrocketing energy prices and heightened insecurity in its southern neighbourhood.
insights.speaker: Majda Ruge
insights.so_what: Europe absorbs the worst of both: reduced US security backing in the east and an energy-price shock from the Iran war.
insights.quote: Primacists have prevailed on Iran—to Europe’s detriment, with skyrocketing energy prices and heightened insecurity in its southern neighbourhood.

insights.claim: Factionalism around Trump is likely to intensify for the rest of his term as the Republican succession battle heats up, with friction most visible in US defence posture in Europe, where the administration seeks to shed security responsibilities while keeping hegemonic privileges.
insights.speaker: Majda Ruge
insights.so_what: Expect continued uncertainty over US troop levels in Europe through 2028, supporting European defence spending.
insights.locator: The factionalism around Trump will likely intensify

insights.claim: The hybrid of the three tribes' visions hurts Europe more than any single one, keeping it in perpetual dependence on a volatile ally.
insights.speaker: Majda Ruge
insights.so_what: Strengthens the case for European strategic autonomy and defence-industrial build-out.
insights.quote: it is the hybrid of these visions that will hurt Europe the most
insights.locator: None of the three tribes’ visions

themes.theme: Prioritisers' setbacks and pivot to Europe

insights.claim: Prioritisers such as J.D. Vance and Elbridge Colby argue deterring China over Taiwan requires all US resources, so Europe should defend itself, but Trump has preferred striking deals with Xi Jinping, leaving the Pentagon preparing for China competition while the president seeks accommodation with Beijing.
insights.speaker: Majda Ruge
insights.so_what: A split between Pentagon planning and presidential deal-making creates unpredictability in US-China policy, relevant for Taiwan risk pricing.
insights.quote: the Pentagon wants to prepare for competition with China while Trump searches for accommodation with Beijing

insights.claim: For prioritisers, the Iran war has been even worse: another massive Middle Eastern commitment that sucks resources from Asia and has drained American military readiness.
insights.speaker: Majda Ruge
insights.so_what: Depleted US readiness raises demand for munitions replenishment and opens space for European defence industry.
insights.locator: If you are a prioritiser, the war in Iran

insights.claim: If Vance or another prioritiser wins the White House, groundwork for a larger US pivot from Europe to Asia will already have been laid, especially if the Pentagon uses allies' own questionnaire answers to depict them as expensive, hostile to US defence firms and unreliable.
insights.speaker: Majda Ruge
insights.so_what: A 2028 prioritiser presidency would accelerate US force reductions in Europe.

themes.theme: The Pentagon questionnaire to NATO allies

insights.claim: In summer 2026 the Pentagon sent NATO allies a questionnaire ostensibly on readiness to backfill future US withdrawals, but it also asked how much they buy from US suppliers, whether they support measures inhibiting transatlantic defence-industrial cooperation, whether they back US Middle East priorities, and whether they restricted US base and airspace access during the Iran war.
insights.speaker: Majda Ruge
insights.so_what: US is linking security presence to purchases of American weapons and political alignment, pressuring 'buy European' defence-industrial policies.
insights.locator: This summer the Pentagon sent a questionnaire

insights.claim: Primacists such as Marco Rubio push Europe to keep buying from US defence firms, and the questionnaire conflated willingness to defend NATO territory with willingness to support a unilateral US war on Iran that damaged European interests.
insights.speaker: Majda Ruge
insights.so_what: Tension between EU defence-industrial preference and US commercial demands is a key variable for US vs European defence contractors.

insights.claim: Europeans are asked to become more capable and less dependent on US forces while remaining politically obedient to an increasingly hostile Washington and commercially dependent on American suppliers.
insights.speaker: Majda Ruge
insights.so_what: Captures the core contradiction of US demands on Europe, implying continued transatlantic friction over defence procurement.
insights.quote: Europeans are being asked to become less dependent on American forces, while remaining obedient to a hostile Washington
insights.locator: Europeans are being asked to become less dependent

insights.claim: Defence secretary Pete Hegseth publicly criticised countries that restricted US base access during the Iran war, warning of consequences, and the questionnaire suggests US presence now depends on whether individual allies fall in line.
insights.speaker: Majda Ruge
insights.so_what: US basing in Europe is becoming transactional, raising risk of punitive relocation for non-aligned allies.
insights.locator: For this, Europeans need to gather all the unity

themes.theme: Europe's new leverage and the need for unity

insights.claim: Europe holds more leverage over the Pentagon's 2026 force-posture review than in January 2025 because the Iran war tied up US high-end assets, Iranian attacks raised the cost of US Gulf basing (making their phase-out more likely), the campaign showed US reliance on European bases and logistics, and depleted US stocks create room for European defence-industrial growth.
insights.speaker: Majda Ruge
insights.so_what: Possible relocation of US capabilities from Gulf bases to Europe, and rising European defence-industrial capacity as US replenishes stockpiles.
insights.quote: Europeans now have more negotiating leverage than they did in January 2025.
insights.locator: The factionalism around Trump will likely intensify

insights.claim: Europe remains heavily dependent on the US for intelligence sharing, missile defence, long-range strike, command and control, nuclear deterrence and weapons supply, so a large-scale US withdrawal would still be very costly.
insights.speaker: Majda Ruge
insights.so_what: These capability gaps define where European defence spending must flow (missile defence, long-range strike, C2).

insights.claim: Europeans failed strategically by sending 27 different responses to the Pentagon questionnaire; if Spain refuses base access for Iran operations but Romania agrees, Washington can simply move bases between countries rather than negotiating with Europe as a bloc.
insights.speaker: Majda Ruge
insights.so_what: Fragmented European positions allow the US to divide and conquer; watch for basing shifts toward compliant eastern-flank states like Romania.
insights.quote: Europeans already failed to act strategically when they sent 27 different responses to the Pentagon’s questionnaire.
insights.locator: Europeans already failed to act strategically

insights.claim: Europe must signal collectively that Washington cannot rescind its core responsibilities if it wants to preserve its hegemonic privileges, and a consolidated European position could influence the US factional struggle itself.
insights.speaker: Majda Ruge
insights.so_what: A unified EU stance on basing and procurement would be a key indicator of Europe's bargaining power with Washington.
